page: Microsoft Azure D32d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. It delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI.

The configuration provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of general-purpose instances (4.0 GB per vCPU). Unlike diskless variants, the D32d_v5 incorporates a dedicated 1288 GB local solid-state drive for low-latency scratch space and temporary file operations. The instance does not include integrated GPU hardware, and complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses are not bundled.

Benchmark measurements position the D32d_v5 solidly within the middle tier across standard compute metrics, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 13741.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 36837.52. Multi-threaded decompression through bzip3 attains 141.75 GB/sec, while software compilation via Clang reaches a score of 26093.0. In memory and cache evaluations, cached small-block reads achieve 1667.63 GB/sec, transitioning to 134.84 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks and 63.71 GB/sec for uncached writes. Static web throughput registers at 31.29 GB/sec alongside 29.76 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance delivers consistent compute efficiency for dense parallel workloads, though execution speeds degrade significantly on memory-intensive large language models such as 70B parameter architectures. The presence of fast local SSD storage combined with 128 GB RAM makes the D32d_v5 a practical fit for relational database management systems, caching layers, software compilation farms, CI/CD runners, and enterprise web application hosting.
description: Microsoft Azure D32d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 128 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory profile. The instance features 1288 GB of local SSD storage for high-speed scratch space, though it lacks discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark results reflect dependable mid-tier performance across varied workloads, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 36837.52, 29.76 million Redis SET operations per second, and 31.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU instruction support includes AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, which benefit multi-threaded compression and build tasks like Clang software compilation. The D32d_v5 provides a reliable baseline for enterprise web application tiers, relational databases requiring fast temporary tables, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed in-memory data stores.
